description: §19.10.5 / §8.9.2 "Amendment S474" item 3 — a `!` server function whose `?{}` queries put its body in the implicit envelope AND which contains an explicit `transaction { }` block compiles clean: the block runs as a SAVEPOINT within the envelope. Until S479 this pinned E-BATCH-001, which S474 retired from the language (g-impl1-retired-batch-codes-still-emitted-s474). It returns a scalar (`return 1;`, §7.2.2 rule 1): the pre-S479 `return { a, b }` had no `;`, and its object literal had no struct type. The deprecated `server` annotation is kept on purpose (a warning, W-DEPRECATED-SERVER-MODIFIER): `both` has no caller, and without it impl#1 reads the function as dead (W-DEAD-FUNCTION) and never judges its envelope, so the impl#1 pin would hold vacuously. Source-reachable since S450 (before it, `transaction { }` did not parse in a function body — see ../implicit-tx-explicit-begin/NOTES.md gap #1).
rationale: §19.10.5: "An explicit `transaction { }` block in a `!` server body — written there or in a function it calls — SHALL run as a SAVEPOINT within the implicit envelope (S474, §8.9.2 "Amendment S474" item 3). Its commit releases the savepoint and its rollback rolls back to it; neither ends the envelope. E-BATCH-001 is retired from the language (§34)." impl#1 still emits the retired code (g-impl1-retired-batch-codes-still-emitted-s474, carried under the S471 impl#1 policy).
